title: Hostel
goal: Check in at the hostel and solve the problem with your missing booking.
twist: The hostel can't find your booking, and tonight's private rooms are full. You negotiate a different room or date.
note: Fictional dialogue constructed for teaching purposes. Harbour Hostel is fictional.

start.speaker: Narrator
start.line: It's evening. You booked a private room at Harbour Hostel for three nights. Your booking number is HC4719. You go to reception.

greet.speaker: Leo
greet.line: Hi, welcome to Harbour Hostel. Are you checking in?
greet.slower: Hello. Do you want to check in?

options.text: Yes, hi. I have a booking under the name Rossi.
options.feedback: Perfect check-in phrase. 'Under the name ...' tells Leo what to look for.

options.text: Obviously. Room, please.
options.feedback: 'Obviously' sounds sarcastic, and Leo still needs your name.
options.recast: Yes, please. I have a booking under the name Rossi.

options.text: Yes, I did a reservation with name Rossi.
options.feedback: Understood. English says 'make a reservation' (not 'do'), or 'I have a booking under the name Rossi'.
options.recast: Yes, I made a reservation under the name Rossi.

whatname.speaker: Leo
whatname.line: Sure. What name is the booking under?

spellname.speaker: Leo
spellname.line: And how do you spell that?
spellname.slower: Please say the letters of your name.

options.text: R, O, double S, I. Rossi.
options.feedback: Clear. 'Double S' is the natural way to spell two of the same letter.

options.text: It's Rossi. Everybody knows how to spell Rossi.
options.feedback: Leo asks so there is no mistake. Not everyone knows how a name is spelled.

options.text: Is R, O, S, S, I.
options.feedback: Leo understands. Start with 'It's ...', or just say the letters.
options.recast: It's R, O, double S, I.

notfound.speaker: Leo
notfound.line: Hmm. I'm sorry, I can't find a booking under that name for tonight. When did you book?
notfound.slower: Sorry. Your booking is not on my computer. When did you book the room?

build.prompt: Say you booked online last week and show your confirmation email.

nearMisses.feedback: 'Last week' is in the past, so use the past simple: 'I booked it'.
'Last week' is in the past, so use the past simple: 'I booked it'.

build.hint: Past time, so use the past simple. Then give your evidence.

options.text: I booked it online last week. Here's my confirmation email.
options.feedback: Calm and helpful. You gave the details and evidence Leo needs.

options.text: That's impossible. Your system is useless.
options.feedback: Grammatical, but angry and blaming. It makes it harder for Leo to help you.
options.recast: Really? I booked it online last week. Can you check again?

options.text: I book it before one week on internet.
options.feedback: Use the past simple ('booked') and 'a week ago' or 'last week'. And say 'online'.
options.recast: I booked it online a week ago.

calm.speaker: Leo
calm.line: I understand it's frustrating. I want to help. Do you have the booking confirmation?

checking.speaker: Leo
checking.line: Let me see. Booking HC4719. Ah, I see the problem. Your booking starts tomorrow, not tonight. And tonight all our private rooms are full.
checking.slower: Your booking is for tomorrow. Tonight there are no private rooms.
checking.spell: H, C, four, seven, one, nine.

options.text: Oh no. Is there another room available tonight?
options.feedback: Good. You accepted the facts and asked for a solution.

options.text: Sorry, could you repeat that? It starts tomorrow?
options.feedback: Good repair. Dates are important, so it's smart to check.

options.text: I want a private room tonight. That's not my problem.
options.feedback: You can be firm, but this ignores the facts. Ask what is possible instead.
options.recast: I really need somewhere to sleep tonight. What can you offer?

options.text: There is other room for tonight?
options.feedback: Question word order: 'Is there another room ...?' Use 'another' with a singular noun.
options.recast: Is there another room for tonight?

repeatdate.speaker: Leo
repeatdate.line: Yes. Your booking starts tomorrow, the fourteenth. Tonight is the thirteenth.

full.speaker: Leo
full.line: I'm sorry, the private rooms really are full. But I might have another option.

offer.speaker: Leo
offer.line: I have one bed in a shared room tonight, a six-bed dormitory. Then you can move to your private room tomorrow.
offer.slower: Tonight you can sleep in a room with five other people. Tomorrow you get your own room.
offer.spell: Dormitory: D, O, R, M, I, T, O, R, Y. A room with many beds.

options.text: I don't mind sharing a room for one night. Would it be possible to pay the dorm price tonight?
options.feedback: Excellent negotiation. You accepted the offer and politely asked for a fair price.

options.text: That works for me. Thank you.
options.feedback: A clear, friendly agreement. You could also ask about the price.

options.text: A dormitory? Absolutely not. I'm not a student.
options.feedback: Grammatical, but it sounds insulting to the guests and to Leo. You can say no politely.
options.recast: Sorry, I'd prefer not to share. Is there anything else?

options.text: Is okay for me sleep in the dormitory.
options.feedback: Understood. Say 'It's OK for me to sleep ...' or, more naturally, 'I don't mind sharing.'
options.recast: It's OK for me to sleep in the dormitory.

otherdate.speaker: Leo
otherdate.line: OK. The other option is a hotel nearby, but it's more expensive. Or the dormitory tonight and your room from tomorrow. What would you prefer?
otherdate.slower: You can go to a hotel. It costs more. Or sleep in the shared room tonight. Which one?

options.text: OK, I'll take the dormitory tonight, then the private room tomorrow.
options.feedback: Good decision, clearly said. You compared the options and chose.

options.text: You choose. I don't care any more.
options.feedback: Leo can't decide for you, and 'I don't care' sounds rude. Make a choice.
options.recast: Hmm. I'll take the dormitory for tonight.

options.text: I prefer the dormitory than the hotel.
options.feedback: With 'prefer', use 'to': 'I prefer the dormitory to the hotel.'
options.recast: I prefer the dormitory to the hotel.

deal.speaker: Leo
deal.line: Sure. I'll charge you the dorm price for tonight, and your private room is ready from tomorrow at two o'clock. Does that work for you?
deal.slower: Tonight you pay less. Tomorrow at two you get your room. Is that OK?

options.text: That works for me. Thanks for sorting it out.
options.feedback: A friendly close. You agreed and thanked Leo for his help.

options.text: So I pay the dorm price tonight, and the room is ready at two tomorrow. Is that right?
options.feedback: Smart. You checked the deal before you agreed.

options.text: Fine. But I'm writing a bad review.
options.feedback: Leo solved the problem, so this sounds unfair. Feedback is fine; threats are not.

options.text: It's work for me.
options.feedback: The phrase is 'That works for me' ('work' is a verb here).

confirmdeal.speaker: Leo
confirmdeal.line: Exactly right. Here's your key for tonight. Bed number three.

end.speaker: Narrator
end.line: You have a bed for tonight, a fair price, and your private room from tomorrow.
end.summary: Task complete: booking problem explained, alternative negotiated, deal confirmed.
